PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp Reports Solid Growth in Quarterly Results

PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, a prominent provider of oilfield services in the United Arab Emirates, reported robust quarterly earnings on Thursday, citing increased demand for upstream support activities in the region as a primary driver of growth.

For the quarter ended March 31, the company posted revenues of AED 1.27 billion, up 7.5% from AED 1.18 billion in the same period a year earlier. Net profit rose to AED 156 million, marking an 11% increase from last year’s AED 141 million. The company credited new contracts and expanded service offerings in offshore engineering and maintenance as key contributors to its improved performance.

“We are pleased with our financial results, which reflect strong execution and continued trust from our clients in the UAE’s dynamic energy sector,” said Nguyen Van Thanh, Chief Executive Officer of PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, during an investor call. “Our focus on operational efficiency and safety standards has positioned us well to capture new opportunities as the market recovers.”

Analysts noted that the company benefited from ongoing infrastructure investments by national oil firms, as well as a steady pace of exploration and production activity in the Persian Gulf. “PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp’s results are a testament to resilient demand for high-quality technical services,” said Noor Al-Khatib, energy analyst at Castorene Capital Advisors. “Their diversified service portfolio and strong relationships with major industry players have insulated them from some of the volatility seen elsewhere in the sector.”

The company’s board proposed an interim dividend of AED 0.18 per share, in line with last year’s payout. Shares of PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp closed up 2.3% on the Dubai Financial Market following the announcement.

Looking ahead, Nguyen indicated the company would continue to invest in workforce training and digitalization initiatives to enhance service delivery. “We remain committed to supporting the UAE’s energy ambitions while maintaining our focus on sustainable growth,” he said.

Industry observers expect regional oilfield services firms to maintain steady growth, supported by favorable oil prices and ongoing project activity across the Gulf.
